name: Noam Chomsky
role: American linguist, philosopher and political critic (MIT and University of Arizona)
summary: An anarchist-leaning critic of the US state, capitalism and the mainstream media, who advocates libertarian socialism with workers' councils and direct participation. He opposes Leninist vanguard parties, US military interventions and corporate power, and has argued for a two-state settlement on international-consensus terms in Israel-Palestine while defending free expression for offensive views.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Calls free-market ideology a fantasy that conceals concentrated power, without denying that markets can allocate resources.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Criticises Reagan-era tax cuts for the wealthy as taxing the poor to pay the rich; does not state a rate.

unions-good.rationale: Describes labour unions as one of the classic ways isolated people can join together to enter the political system, and has long defended union rights.

property-fundamental.rationale: Opposes private ownership of the means of production as incompatible with free labour, so does not treat such property as fundamental.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Criticises corporate power over government and media, but is not recorded as backing specific regulatory measures.

worker-ownership.rationale: Argues that a consistent anarchist must oppose private ownership of the means of production and wants producers to control production collectively.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Criticises the creation of a surveillance state and argues that privacy should not have to be defended.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Defends free expression of ideas, even offensive ones, and opposed restricting the speech of Faurisson.

state-harmful.rationale: As an anarchist, calls for finishing with the state and dismantling authority that is no longer justified.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Relies on the UN Charter as the basis of international law and criticises US blocking of UN action, without stating a view on more UN power.

free-trade.rationale: Criticises so-called free trade agreements such as NAFTA as protecting corporate and intellectual-property interests rather than free exchange.

nation-first.rationale: Criticises the United States for pursuing its own interests above international law, though not as an explicit rejection of national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Argues that claimed humanitarian interventions are usually cynical pretexts, so does not accept the principle as a general justification.

limit-growth.rationale: Supports the principles of degrowth but says degrowth is not a solution on its own, so the position is mixed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls for urgent, large-scale government action on climate change, including through a Green New Deal.

revolution-justified.rationale: Regards violent revolution as a last resort to be avoided where possible, which implies it can sometimes be justified.

central-planning.rationale: Criticises bureaucratic, autocratic control of the economy by the state and by Leninist parties as the opposite of socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Favours producer and community control of production within an economy that remains partly market-based, but does not address markets themselves.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Calls wage slavery incompatible with a free society and wants labour freely undertaken; does not address money itself.

one-party-rule.rationale: Criticises single-party Leninist states as bureaucratic systems and the exact antithesis of socialism.

direct-votes.rationale: Favours direct participation in decisions rather than representative government alone, through councils and general assemblies.

workers-councils.rationale: Advocates government by workers' councils as the basis of a libertarian socialist society.

political-violence-never.rationale: Regards violent revolution as a last resort, so does not accept that political violence is never justified.

military-superiority.rationale: Criticises US military dominance of the world and its use of force abroad.

direct-action.rationale: Supports direct action such as demonstrations and boycotts against corporations as one tactic among many.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Quotes anarchist critiques of private ownership as exploitation of the weak by the strong; does not state the labour-theory claim in his own words.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Sceptical of a violent dictatorship of the proletariat led by self-appointed vanguard parties.

total-state.rationale: Opposes state totalitarianism and state socialism, and favours direct participation over state direction.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Accepts that both national groups have a right to self-determination but rejects a 'right to exist' as a concept in international law.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Advocates direct worker control of production and government by workers' councils, with a democratic say in how economic institutions are run.

national-self-determination.rationale: Argues that both national groups in Palestine have the right to national self-determination and that the US has blocked a settlement on that basis.

force-without-un.rationale: Describes the UN Charter limits on force (Security Council authorisation or self-defence against an armed attack) and criticises NATO's action in Kosovo as outside them.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposes apartheid and the legal segregation of races, calling Israel's treatment of Palestinians worse than South Africa's.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposes expanding shale gas and fossil-fuel energy plans given the climate threat.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Treats settler colonialism as the cruelest form of imperialism and says the concept applies to Palestine before 1948.

vanguard-party.rationale: Criticises the vanguard party model of Leninism as an autocratic elite controlling the working class.

party-controls-media.rationale: Calls for grassroots democratic control and involvement of the media rather than control by a government or party.

recall-officials.rationale: Favours revocable representatives in principle, but the recall of elected officials is not separately addressed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Criticises NATO expansion as a provocation and opposes a stronger NATO.

death-penalty.rationale: States that the application of the death penalty is inherently bad and wrong, and opposes it in all countries.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Supports a two-state settlement on internationally recognised borders and opposes Israel retaining occupied territory.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Calls Israel's rule in the occupied territories an occupation and criticises settlements as illegal; not a general principle on annexation.

refugee-return.rationale: Rejects the right of return as a demographic threat to Israel in 2005, but says settlements must address refugee return or compensation under UN resolutions.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Argues that the mass media mostly distract the public and marginalise dissent, reproducing the existing order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Argues that power is maintained by manufacturing consent through the media and institutions, not mainly by force.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Favours temporary and revocable representatives chosen by councils and general assemblies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Argues that corporate and financial interests control government and media, with the two major US parties serving a business party.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Advocates direct participation by ordinary people in workplaces and communities, and in the government of affairs.

alienated-labor.rationale: Draws on Marx's account of alienated labour and argues that wage labour denies workers the creative control of their work.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Argues that corporate ownership of the mass media constrains what is reported, and calls for grassroots democratic control of media.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Describes a carbon tax as one way to address emissions, while noting that it would face industry opposition.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Calls for finishing with the state in a revolution, though his position on the form of the transition is not spelled out.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Describes Tobin's proposal to tax speculative currency flows as a way to slow flows that would otherwise drive a low-wage economy; does not state his own endorsement outright.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Argues that unpleasant and unpopular jobs could be fully automated, as a means of reducing work.

notes: Positions are drawn from his own articles and interviews on chomsky.info plus Wikipedia as a reference. Coverage is strongest on economy, government, world affairs and the media. Israel-Palestine: his stated preference shifted over decades (a binational or one-state option in the 1970s-2000s, a two-state international-consensus settlement by 2023), so the 2023 interview is taken as the most recent clear view. Faurisson: he defended the right of expression, and his 1980 essay does not endorse Faurisson's claims. Wikipedia reports a 2023 stroke with loss of ability to speak or walk, so no newer positions are recorded. Books (Understanding Power, Requiem for the American Dream, Who Rules the World?, Hegemony or Survival) were not downloaded separately; the chomsky.info texts used include the book-related talks and interviews. 'Government in the Future' (1970) was not found in the chomsky.info index. Most statements are null because the corpus does not address them.
